andy: Heads up — saw a 2x tail latency blip on prod-gpu-pool at 12:03 UTC. NSYS trace attached. Root shows big queue wait before attention kernels.

maria: Which model / seq distribution? Can you drop the nsys id or paste the hot timeline?

andy: Model: gpt-xl-replica, typical seq ~512. Spike came from a mixed batch (seqs 8, 16, 512, 1024). NSYS capture: s3://bench/1959123456/nsys.cp

perf-bot: nsys capture processed -> link: https://perf-storage/reports/1959123456 (summary: long host-side gaps, multiple kernel fallsbacks)

sam: Quick read of the timeline: we see continuous-batching windows grouping small and large seqs. After window close, KV cache sweep runs and we get a host sync. Snippet from perfetto-like summary:

```
window_open: 0.0ms
queue_time: 18.2ms
compute_time: 3.1ms
KV_SWEEP: 26.7ms  <-- host sync, forces kernel fallback path
window_close: 48.0ms
```

sam: So queue_time >> compute_time; batching helps throughput but this sync amplifies tail p99.

cheng: From kernel-selection logic: we pick `attn_v2` for seq <= 256, else `attn_fallback` (more general). For mixed batches the runtime currently picks the conservative kernel based on max seq in the batch which pushes mem copies + different launch config.

lena: That explains compute jump. Also noticed KV cache invalidation / sweep is unconditional at window close which triggers host-side memory ops if there are recently-evicted KV shards.

andy: Hypothesis: mixed-seq batching + unconditional KV sweep -> kernel fallback & host sync -> queue tail spike.

maria: Proposed mitigation: 1) bucket continuous-batching windows by seq range so we don't mix tiny & huge sequences in same kernel launch. 2) gate KV sweep behind a threshold: skip if avg_seq < X or make it lazy.

sam: Quick experiment: ran a patched scheduler that splits windows into buckets (<=64, 65-256, >256) and added `runtime.kv.sweep_threshold=128` to skip sweep on short batches. Re-ran nsys capture (id 1959123480). Results:

```
baseline p99: 254ms
patched p99:   198ms  (~22% improvement)
GPU util: 78% -> 91%
observed host->device gaps reduced by ~30%
```

cheng: Nice. Also note kernel-selection change: when buckets are homogeneous, we consistently pick `attn_v2` for small batches and avoid the heavier fallback. That reduces memory thrash and the matmul kernels get better occupancy.

lena: We should also adjust `batch_close_timeout` heuristics to prefer earlier flush for tiny sequences when a large seq arrives, instead of forcing them into a long window.

andy: Can someone open a small PR with: bucketed-window scheduling, `runtime.kv.sweep_threshold` (default 128), and an NVTX marker around KV sweep so we can detect it in future traces?

maria: I'll take the PR. Will include unit/perf test that simulates mixed seq workload and asserts p99 improvement and no regression on throughput.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled for 03:00 UTC tomorrow. Watching metrics: p50/p95/p99, GPU idle gaps, KV sweep frequency.

andy: Thanks — after canary we can decide if sweep should be async or fully lazy (background thread). Keep nsys links in thread for triage.

lena: Also adding an alert: if queue_time / compute_time > 4x for 1min -> page eng-runtime oncall.

maria: ack. I'll include the perf summary and timeline snapshots in the PR description.

andy: Great work. Short action items: maria PR, sam extra nsys with NVTX, cheng validate kernel affinity impact, lena add alert. We'll review results post-canary.
